title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC0LE_1RD0LB_0RA1RC_0RC0RF_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC0LE_1RD0LB_0RA1RC_0RC0RF_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; the machine is conjectured not to halt. Its run is a rewriting of a list of runs of 1s; the cycle rule and every epoch-end rule seen are proved in Lean for all parameters, none of them halts, and an accelerated simulation built on them runs 8,000 epochs (about 108021 steps) without a halt. A complete set of rules for arbitrary run lists is not yet written.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 90,021 cells have been visited and 55,564 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504).

claims.title: The cycle rule
claims.text: With the head in state A just right of the tape, L 1^(a+3) (01)^(b+1) A> becomes L 1^a (01)^(b+6) A> in 6b+45 steps, for all a, b and every tape L: the last run of 1s loses 3 cells and 5 units (single 1s) appear.

claims.title: The epoch-end rules
claims.text: When the active run has 0 or 2 cells left: an empty run takes one cell from its left neighbour and turns the B units into a run of 2B+11 (q0_unit, q0_long, units_blank); a run of 2 after a long run takes 3 from it, adds 7 units and turns the units into a run of 2B−1 (q2_long); after an empty run or blank tape the units before it become a run of 2m+4 or 2m+6, then 6 units, then 2B−5 (q2_zero, q2_blank). All for all parameters.

claims.title: 8,000 epochs without a halt
claims.text: An exact accelerated simulator (run-length tape with the shift rules of bbtools.symtm, and the proved cycle rule applied k times at once) runs 8,000 epochs from blank tape, about 108021 steps, without a halt. Its tape agrees cell for cell with the C simulator at the start of each of the first 8 epochs (to step 3,197,349,547).

claims.title: No halting piece in a symbolic class search
claims.text: A class is the tape … 1^n 0 0 A> in which n and every other run or block of at least 20 words are free. A symbolic simulator runs each class to the next such tape for all values at once, splitting it into pieces when the outcome depends on a residue or on the order of two counts. In 15 minutes: 2,517 classes, 67,561 pieces, every piece reaches a node, none halts, none is undecided. The set is not closed: 555 classes were still queued and the list of runs keeps getting longer. A plain simulator agrees on a random sample of 200 classes (8,165 piece runs).

claims.title: Why it should not halt
claims.text: A halt needs state A moving right onto 1 1 1. In every rule A moving right meets only units and the run of 2 itself. The residues mod 3 that choose the branch look random (2,634 / 2,629 / 2,737 in 8,000 epochs), and the runs left of the active one stayed small (one long run of at most 32 and one block of units).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known, conjectured no. Missing for a proof: the general rule for an active run of 2 right after a run of 2 (a recursion further left), and a closed set of run lists covering every epoch end; with all residues allowed the runs left of the active one can grow without bound, so a finite enumeration does not close.

explainer.lede: Probably never, but nobody has proved it. This machine keeps a list of runs of 1s on its tape. It eats the last long run three cells at a time, leaving a trail of single 1s, and when the run is used up, the remainder mod 3 decides how the trail is turned into a new run, about 10/3 times longer than the old one.

facts.text: One cycle: the last long run loses 3 cells, 5 single 1s appear (proved for all lengths).
8,000 epochs simulated exactly with the proved rules, no halt.
Growth of the active run from one epoch to the next.
No halt in the C simulator; 90,021 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A list of runs, eaten from the right
html: Stop the machine whenever the head, in state A, has just stepped past the last written cell, and read the tape as runs of 1s separated by single 0s. A run of length 1 is a unit (write u^k for k of them); two 0s side by side are an empty run. The tape always looks like

with one long active run of a ones and B units after it. One cycle: the head walks left over the units, bites 3 cells off the active run, and walks back writing 5 new units. So [a] u^B becomes [a−3] u^(B+5), a theorem in Lean for every a and B.

The cycles go on until the active run has 0, 1 or 2 cells left, so the end of an epoch is decided by a mod 3:

• 1 left: it is a unit now, and the next long run to the left becomes active.
  • 0 left: the run to the left gives up one cell, and the B units are filled in to one new run of 2B+11 ones.
  • 2 left: the run to the left gives up 3 cells (or, if there is none, the units before it are packed into a run), 7 units are added there, and the B units become a new run of 2B−1.

B grew by 5 for every 3 cells eaten, so the new run is about (10/3)·a. Each epoch the tape gets 10/3 times longer and takes about 11 times as many steps: that is the square-root growth of the tape in the picture below. The epochs from blank tape (py/epochs.py):

epoch  3  step       21,645   4 u^6 [338] u^3        338 mod 3 = 2
epoch  4  step      216,882   u^14 [1122] u^3        1122 mod 3 = 0
epoch  5  step    2,338,267   u^13 [3753] u^3        3753 mod 3 = 0
epoch  6  step   25,890,901   u^12 [12523] u^3       12523 mod 3 = 1
epoch  7  step  287,483,938   [41778] u^3            (all units merged)
...
epoch 14  step     ~10^15     32 u^4 [191048923] u^3
epoch 15  step     ~10^16     [32] u^318414878       (the old run 32 is active again)

sections.heading: Can it ever stop?
html: The machine stops only in state F reading a 1, which can only happen when state A, moving right, runs into three 1s in a row. In every rule above A moving right meets only units, or the run of 2 at an epoch end (then F reads the 0 after it: three such near misses happen in the first 109 steps). None of the rules halts, and 8,000 epochs, about 108021 steps, were simulated exactly without a halt.

What keeps this from being a proof: the remainders mod 3 behave like coin flips, and an unlucky sequence of them could build a longer list of runs to the left of the active one, which leads to cases (a run of 2 right after a run of 2) whose general rule recurses and has not been written out. A proof needs a rule for every possible run list, or an argument that those sequences never come.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504).
After 109 steps the tape spans 90,021 cells (12 left of the start, 70,310 right), with a density of 1s of 0.617.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LA0LE_0RA0RF_1RC---: rename A→C, B→D, C→A, D→B, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB---_1RC1RE_1LD0LE_1RF0LC_0RD0RA_0RB1RD: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→F, E→E, F→A; it is this table started in state F
  • 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD1LB_1LA1LE_0LB0LF_1LD---: rename A→D, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

summary: Nested run counter: the last long run of 1s is eaten 3 cells at a time while 5 units appear; at the end of each epoch its residue mod 3 rewrites the runs to its left and the units become a run 10/3 times longer. No halting case found; 8,000 epochs (~10^8021 steps) simulated.
family: nested run counter, x10/3 per epoch (mod-3 branching)
